extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent agents/attorneys, and drafters preparing patent specifications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting patent specifications: what to disclose, how to describe machines/substances/combinations, use of drawings, distinguishing new from old, and duty to disclose best mode and workable means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire_consideration_rule (multiple claimed inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is taken out for many different things, the entire discovery of all those things is the consideration upon which the crown is induced to make the grant; and, if that consideration fails in any part, it fails in toto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming several distinct inventions in one patent, beware that lack of novelty or failure as to any one claimed thing may render the whole patent void (cases: Hill v. Thompson; Bayley, J.). Prefer separate patents or ensure the claimed items form a proper single subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: No_unnecessary_or_useless_parts
rubrics_metrics.description: If useless and unnecessary things have been put into a specification (mixed with a substance or attached to a machine) though the terms are intelligible and necessary description introduced, the patent is void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including components that are never used or unnecessary to produce the desired effect raises a presumption they were inserted to mislead the public (example: Arkwright's machine). Avoid listing extraneous elements that are not part of the invention; if included, explain their role and why they are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_listing_many_alternatives_without_pointing_out_workable_one
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must not give several ways and methods which may or may not answer, leaving the public to use those they please, if only one will answer the intended purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enumerate many substitutes or salts/ingredients if only one actually works; specifying many alternatives without identifying which produces the effect can make the specification incorrect or void (example: Turner's patent with many salts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do_not_claim_effects_that_cannot_be_produced
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee should inform the enquirer of the exact nature of the manufacture invented; if the article described has not the qualities, or the machine produce not the results set forth in the specification, the grant is invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claimed properties and results are accurate and demonstrably producible by the disclosed methods; overstatements of capability risk invalidation (examples: Winter's multiple promised outputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best_mode_disclosure_duty
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subject be not given to the public in the best and most improved state known to the inventor at the time of obtaining the grant, the patent is void; concealment of a mode known to the inventor is fraudulent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the best method of practicing the invention known at filing (examples: omission of tempering with tallow for 'steel trusses', omission of aqua fortis for verdigris). Any advantageous operation known to inventor that was concealed may render the patent void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent_discovery_exception
rubrics_metrics.description: If a better mode of using the manufacture is a subsequent discovery (found after the date of the grant), then the grant will continue valid; but a presumption of concealment is against the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between improvements known before filing (must be disclosed) and those discovered later (may be used). Be prepared to show chronology if accused of concealment (case: Boville/Brown discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent_omission_and_fraud_presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: An omission, even if inadvertent, may render the patent void if the patentee actually knew and meant to practice the omitted mode; the patentee must answer for inadvertence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully review specifications to avoid accidental omission of known beneficial modes; courts treat inadvertence skeptically where the inventor knew the omitted information (case: Boville v. Moore).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings_optional_but_must_enable_construction_when_used
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not absolutely necessary to annex a model, diagram, picture, or drawing; if without it the subject is clearly described it is better omitted. If a drawing is introduced it should illustrate parts; if it enables a workman of ordinary skill to construct the improvement, it is as good as any written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use drawings to clarify complex parts, but ensure drawings are sufficiently detailed to allow a skilled workman to build the invention; earlier strict scale requirements have been relaxed where a common mechanic can make the subject from a perspective drawing (Arkwright example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification_level_of_detail_for_machines
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of a machine must disclose the nature of the invention and the manner in which it is to be performed; when it descends to particulars, elements known to all should not be noticed nor include anything unnecessary; it should enable a common mechanic of reasonable skill to comprehend it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide dimensions, proportions (diameters, lengths, thickness, tensions), relative velocities and methods of uniting parts where necessary. Do not require the reader to have only elementary knowledge of mechanics; do not demand inventive faculty to practice the disclosure. The jury decides what constitutes reasonable skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: No_resort_to_essential_experiments_or_trials
rubrics_metrics.description: No contrivance or addition, no trial or experiment must be resorted to for a full knowledge of the invention; if the inventor leaves anything to be found out by experiment the specification is bad unless data and manner are clearly given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient parameters and expected results so that reproduction does not require inventive trials; non-essential trials may be acceptable if adequate data is supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit_references_to_scientific_books
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference may be made to the rudiments of the science by which the principles are explained, but not to scientific books; a proposition generally known needs no reference; that which can be found only in some particular treatise must be explained but not claimed as new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on external treatises to supply necessary enabling information; include explanations for any specialized knowledge required to perform the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe_removable_or_variable_parts_and_uses
rubrics_metrics.description: If parts of the machine are to be put on and off during some operations, or if several articles are intended to be worked on, it must be distinctly stated what those parts are, their proportions for different purposes, and where they are to be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invention involves interchangeable parts or multiple operational modes, explicitly describe each configuration, proportions, and applicable uses to enable correct practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do_not_claim_more_than_the_invention (improvements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant must not be more extensive than the invention; where the patent is for an improvement or addition, the inventor cannot monopolize the whole subject; the specification is incorrect if it contains description of more than the improvement unless it particularly distinguishes the new from the old parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When patenting an improvement, clearly identify and limit claims to new elements or combinations; distinguish old/background components so as not to claim pre-existing subject matter (cases: Williams v. Brodie; Macfarlane v. Price).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible_ways_to_describe_improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Several acceptable methods exist for describing an improvement: (1) describe the whole manufacture then particularize the addition; (2) describe the whole and point out parts that are old or not material; (3) give an accurate description of the improvement and how it is applied to the old parts; (4) describe the whole manufacture and refer to the prior patent specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the describing method that makes the new contribution intelligible without undue burden on the public; when referring to prior patents, ensure references are clear and, where practical, mark new vs old parts distinctly (cases cited in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: When_to_refer_to_prior_or_expired_specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the combination consists of subjects of several expired patents or previously known parts, a description of the method by which they are combined, with reference to the several specifications, may be sufficient to sustain the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may cite and combine prior patented subjects (especially expired ones), but clearly state the novel aspect — the new combination or application — and provide sufficient information on how the combination operates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim_only_new_combinations_or_new_conformation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the novelty consists in a new conformation or in new combinations of known parts, the patentee may claim the composition if the combination from the beginning is his invention; but if earlier combinations existed up to a point and the patentee only added beyond that, claiming the whole machine may be bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully analyze prior combinations and claim only the genuinely novel structural configuration or added combinations. Courts will examine whether the patentee's contribution is merely an improvement of an existing engine or a wholly new machine (case: Brown/Boville/Jessop discussions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do_not_include_more_old_material_without_designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every old part which is essential and material in producing the intended effect will be considered as claimed if it is not designated as old; material old elements should be designated to avoid improper claiming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When incorporating old elements into a specification, explicitly identify them as pre-existing to avoid being deemed to claim them as new; failure to mark them may expand claim scope improperly and invalidate the specification.
